advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to test_gate_doc_never_blocks_claims_name_the_escalation_exception so it fails if the claim substring is not found (assert presence before asserting the 'escalat' qualifier).
evidence: tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step7_class_review.py:94-97: `for line in _GATE_DOC.read_text().splitlines(): / if claim in line: / assert "escalat" in line.lower(), (...)`
No liveness/presence anchor asserts the parametrized `claim` was found at all; if `claim in line` is never true the loop completes with zero assertions and the test passes.
Litmus (fail-open): the check yields 'pass' both when the claim is properly qualified AND when the claim line never appears — it cannot distinguish its verdict from the producer not being present.
advisory.finding: test_gate_doc_never_blocks_claims_name_the_escalation_exception passes vacuously (fail-open oracle): it only asserts the 'escalat' qualifier when `claim in line`, so if the never-blocks claim string is reworded or removed the assertion body never runs and the test reports green — the exact regression it exists to catch (an unqualified never-blocks claim) is invisible to it.
scenarios: A future edit rewords 'never blocks a bug' or 'coached but never BLOCKED' (e.g. adds punctuation, splits the line, changes casing) so the substring no longer matches — the guard silently stops enforcing qualification.
A new unqualified never-blocks sentence is added elsewhere with slightly different phrasing — the parametrized substrings miss it and the test is green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track a `found` flag: `found = False; for line in ...: if claim in line: found = True; assert 'escalat' in line.lower(), ...` then `assert found, f"claim not present: {claim!r}"` — so a reworded/removed claim fails the test instead of passing vacuously.
